title: A scene
description: A scene: a set, and the steps played on it, on each of its device types. Anything at the top or in a step can be given again under a device type, and applies only on that type.

$schema.description: The URL of the schema the file is written against, for editors. Optional; a file is read against this Retake's schema whatever it names.

devices.description: The device types it plays on; every one when not given.

set.description: The set the scene starts on; the project's defaultSet when not given.

setup.description: Steps played before recording starts. Nothing anchors to them, so they have no id.

leadIn.description: Seconds recorded before the first step. For a scene that records its launch, they start once the app is reachable, after the launch is recorded.

tail.description: Seconds recorded after the last step.

defaultHold.description: The hold of each step that doesn't give its own.

recordsLaunch.description: Starts recording before the app launches, to catch its launch screen.

orientation.description: The orientation the device is turned to before the app launches.

steps.description: What the scene does, in order.

iphone.description: Overrides for iphone's video, laid over the rest key by key.

leadIn.description: Seconds recorded before the first step. For a scene that records its launch, they start once the app is reachable, after the launch is recorded.

tail.description: Seconds recorded after the last step.

steps.description: What the scene does, in order.

step.description: One thing the scene does, led by what it does, and the pause after it. A step can be only a hold.

tap.description: Touches a point, x and y, or an element. An element is touched at its activation point, which the step log records, so either is drawn in the video.

x.description: Screen points from the left, or a percentage of the screen's width as the device faces.

oneOf.description: A percentage of the screen, such as 50%.

y.description: Screen points from the top, or a percentage of the screen's height as the device faces.

oneOf.description: A percentage of the screen, such as 50%.

drag.description: A straight one-finger drag from one point or element to another. An element is touched at its activation point, as the screen has it just before the drag, moved by its offset and offsetPercent.

from.description: Where the finger comes down: a point, x and y, or an element.

x.description: Screen points from the left, or a percentage of the screen's width as the device faces.

oneOf.description: A percentage of the screen, such as 50%.

y.description: Screen points from the top, or a percentage of the screen's height as the device faces.

oneOf.description: A percentage of the screen, such as 50%.

to.description: Where it lifts: a point, x and y, or an element.

y.description: Screen points from the top, or a percentage of the screen's height as the device faces.

oneOf.description: A percentage of the screen, such as 50%.

type.description: Types text key by key on the on-screen keyboard.

into.description: The element to type into; the field already being typed in when not given.

activate.description: An accessibility activation of an element, with no touch, for getting somewhere off camera.

orientation.description: Turns the device, with no hand on it; the step ends when the app has turned and the device has drawn the rotation.

waitFor.description: Waits until an element is on screen, or with gone until it isn't. The step fails if it doesn't happen in time.

value.description: Its value: a text field's placeholder, or what's typed in it.

identifier.description: The accessibilityIdentifier the app gives it.

hint.description: Its accessibility hint: what VoiceOver says it does.

traits.description: Traits it has, every one, by The Button Heist's names, as `retake compose` prints them.

occurrence.description: Which of several matching elements, counted from 1 in the order VoiceOver reads the screen. A last resort, since it breaks when the layout changes: name the element closely enough, by its traits, identifier, value or hint, that only it matches.

gone.description: Waits for the element to leave instead.

timeout.description: Seconds to wait: at most The Button Heist's longest wait, by default 60 s, which BUTTONHEIST_MAX_WAIT_TIMEOUT raises, set where Retake runs and in the set's environment, for the app.

capture.description: Saves the screen as a still, as it is when the step before has ended and its hold is over, as a PNG named for it in the output directory's captures/<type>/<scene>/, when the scene is recorded. Unique in the scene. Not in setup.

hold.description: Seconds to pause after the step, or for a tap, from when it's sent; the scene's defaultHold when not given.

id.description: The name edits anchor to. Unique in the scene; it can't look like a number, which anchors count steps by, nor be start or end.

devices.description: The device types it plays on; every one when not given. On another, it's skipped but keeps its number, so the steps after it are numbered alike on every type, and nothing can anchor to it there.
